sermon.title: The Nations
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches what the Lord requires, distinguishes shadow, wise, civil and spiritual laws, and applies Israel’s call to possess the land to the church’s call to teach all nations with the word and the Spirit. He insists God shows no partiality, warns that blood-guilt follows silence toward the wicked, and shows from Acts 10 and Romans 2 that every nation's God-fearers who do right are accepted.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Statistic “7.3 billion / seven and a half million / little over ten percent” without food is as spoken and arithmetically inconsistent—flagged unverified. “News olams” captions corrected to Muslims. Named politics (Democrats/Republicans outsourcing), Islam/mosque reciprocity, homosexuality, socialism kept as spoken.

chunks.section_question: What kinds of Bible laws are there?
chunks.short_answer: He distinguishes civil, spiritual, wise and shadow laws. Wise laws include not even looking on wine when it is red in the cup, and not going near a prostitute’s house—wisdom that flees the appearance of evil. Christians under grace are not under shadow laws but still under civil, spiritual and wise laws, and must teach children and grandchildren diligently.

chunks.section_question: How were Israel to possess the land, and how do we possess nations now?

Israel failed when not strong in the word. In the New Testament the sword is the word (Ephesians 6:17); we teach all nations to observe what Christ commanded—not megachurch books—preaching repentance and remission of sins in his name (Luke 24:47).

faqs.question: Is keeping God’s laws meant to make life miserable?
faqs.answer: He says the purpose is for our good, not to hinder enjoyment of life—people twist the Scriptures when they say otherwise.

faqs.question: Do you go to hell for walking by a prostitute’s house?
faqs.answer: He says you don’t go to hell for walking by her house; you go to hell for going in and getting in her bed—the wise law is to avoid.

faqs.question: Are American public schools really public schools?
faqs.answer: He says if they were public they would allow Jewish, Catholic and Protestant Bibles; instead they teach the religion of secular humanism.

faqs.question: Is water baptism our circumcision?
faqs.answer: From Colossians 2 he says water baptism is circumcision made without hands, putting off the body of sin; the old man is dead.

faqs.question: Should America grant equal religious freedom if we are not treated equally abroad?
faqs.answer: He says unless they treat us equally over there, we don’t have to treat them equally here regarding building mosques while churches disappear in those nations.

faqs.question: How many people does he say lack enough food?
faqs.answer: He says of about 7.3 billion, only about seven and a half million—a little over ten percent in his wording—don’t have enough food every day, because God said he would give food and clothing. (Statistic as spoken; unverified.)

faqs.question: What sword do New Testament churches use toward the nations?
faqs.answer: The sword of the Spirit is the word of God—quick, powerful, sharper than any two-edged sword—not guns to force people to serve God.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God;

faqs.question: Why does he say to use the name Jesus, not just “God”?
faqs.answer: He says don’t use the vague word God in this society—use Jesus, the name they hate, because Jesus was God and is identified with Protestant and Catholic religion.

faqs.question: What two things do we need to witness to the nations?
faqs.answer: The power of the word and the power of the Spirit—understanding opened to the Scriptures and being filled with the Holy Ghost.

faqs.question: What is the conscience according to Romans 2?
faqs.answer: The recognition of right and wrong in the thought process—bearing witness, accusing or else excusing—when God judges secrets by Jesus Christ.
